Duduzane Zuma

By: Graham Coetzer | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The president's son has been at the forefront of the news since the release of the Guptaleaks - but who is the man behind the headlines?

Unique Selling Point:
Dudzane Zuma's role in facilitating lucrative government contracts for the Gupta family has been cast into the spotlight as emails released in the Gupta leaks show just how much of a role he's played for the controversial family.

Summary:
The president's young son has had a colourful career, starting of as an intern for the Gupta's in the IT department of Sahara. But company registers and sharholding certificates show a meteoric rise starting in 2007 as his father was elected president. From lucrative shareholdings in Oakbay and it's related company's to Tegeta, a lot of which he seemingly paid nothing for, it is clear his political connections have assured him a life of luxury. The emails also reveal how the Gupta's helped him purchase a multi-million rand mansion in Dubai and secure his sought after residency. He has also been notorious in the media as a young playboy in South Africa, facing scandals in his personal life with extra-marital affairs and a car accident which left one person dead.

Further information:
Will create graphics showing his rise through the Gupta empire. We still have soundbytes from last weeks episode of Sipho Pityana, Ralph Mathekga and David Lewis which are relevant. We will profile Duduzane against the current gloomy econonomic backdrop in SA.

Press Release:


As more details emerge in leaked emails about alleged corrupt business activities relating to state entities and Gupta run companies, Duduzane
Zuma, the President’s son has taken centre stage in the growing controversy. From being just an intern a few years ago to his meteoric rise into
2
powerful positions in numerous Gupta-linked businesses – Zuma has become the man of the moment. So is he just a pawn in the Gupta empire
or the ultimate king maker? Carte Blanche investigates the man behind the headlines.

Script:


Duduzane Zuma
9 June 2017

Voice
In what has been described as one of the most sensational information leaks in South African history, the Guptaleaks emails this week revealed more evidence of the close ties between the Gupta empire and President Jacob Zuma’s 35 year old son Duduzane Zuma. Amongst others, the emails reveal how the Gupta’s paid for Duduzane’s air travel for a Mauritius holiday, helped plan and pay for his wedding, and purchase an R18m luxury apartment in Dubai’s Burj Khalifa, the world’s tallest building. But where did it all begin?

Sound Up Pieter-Louis Myburgh
There’s still some uncertainty as to exactly when President Jacob Zuma and the Gupta’s meet for the very first time. There are sources and reports that point to a friendship having been forged in the nineties already when President Jacob Zuma was still an MEC in Kwazulu-Natal province. And then as we know now in 2001 already he introduces Duduzane his son to the Gupta’s.

Voice
Investigative journalist and author Pieter-Louis Myburgh has written extensively on the Gupta family dealings in South Africa. He says Duduzane was soon working for the Gupta’s Sahara Systems.

Sound Up Pieter-Louis Myburgh
He’s a young man, fresh out of university or school, looking for a job, and that is where the Gupta’s come to his rescue and appoint him in Sahara computers. So it’s interesting, that’s definitely the origin of the Zuma/Gupta relationship as far as Duduzane goes.

Link Devi
According to Duduzane Zuma he joined Sahara Systems at the age of 22 as a trainee. But it was only after his father had been elected as president of the ANC in 2007 that his star began to rise.

Voice
In July 2008 Zuma was appointed a director and acquired 25% shares in Mabengela Investments alongside the younger Gupta brother, Rajesh. He paid R25 for his stake. Over the next two years and four months, Duduzane was appointed as a director in another 11 Gupta companies

Sound Up Pieter-Louis
So it’s very interesting how quickly after Zuma’s rise to power, Duduzane Zuma is given the key to these Gupta riches.


Voice
And most of those riches would come from Mabengela Investments and Islandsite Investments 255, both of which Duduzane Zuma became a director of between 2008-2009.

Link Devi
Duduzane Zuma has a significant shareholding in both these companies, and it seems he paid almost nothing for his shares.

Voice
According to a City Press report Duduzane only paid R45 for his 45% stake in Mabengela. But both Mabengela and Islandsite earned millions in lucrative government contracts.

Sound Up Pieter-Louis
Those two companies start playing a major role, and start becoming a major beneficiary, of these big sort of government deals, and deals that are related to the Gupta’s and deals also most worryingly that President Jacob Zuma would have a say in, in helping to influence.

Voice
These include significant stakes in:
-Shiva Uranium, which parent company Oakbay Resources wanted to have supply uranium to the South African Nuclear programme
- VR Laser that was involved in the lucrative Transnet tender for locomotives valued at R25 billion as well as a joint venture with state arms company Denel
-Tegeta Exploration and Resources and it’s notorious Eskom contracts
-and Infinity Media which owns the Gupta television channel ANN7.

Sound Up Pieter-Louis
The question of an arms-length distance between Duduzane Zuma and president Jacob Zuma and the Gupta’s seems very curious at this juncture.

Voice
According to political analyst Ralph Mathekga the leaks are providing substance to the allegations that Duduzane Zuma might be the ultimate kingmaker in the Gupta saga.

Sound Up Ralph
Duduzane Zuma appears to be South Africa’s super director general, you know managing all the transactions locally that involve the interests of the Gupta family and those that involve the interests of his father, who happens to be the president.

Voice
Mathekga says the president and his son’s appeals that Duduzane is just an ordinary South African are ridiculous.

Sound Up Ralph
The reality is that if you are going into politics as a leader, you get elected to a top position, you cannot expect us to view your family like any other families. You are closer to resources, you are responsible for decisions that determine the direction in which resources are being distributed. So the whole thing of President Jacob Zuma asking that his children be treated as ordinary South Africans is naïve.

Voice
In some of the latest email leaks, Duduzane negotiates with pr firm Bell Pottinger’s Victoria Geoghegan in what reports have described as a series of underhanded tactics to divert public outcry to the Gupta family. According to the communications this would come at a cost of 100 000 pounds a month.

Sound Up Pieter-Louis
The most disturbing detail from the Guptaleaks emails to me personally is the fact that Duduzane Zuma was sent the CV of one Mosebenzi Zwane, by Tony Rajesh Gupta.

Voice
A month later on the 23rd of September 2015, President Jacob Zuma appointed Zwane as the minister of Mineral Resources. The emails also highlight the benefits Duduzane receives from the Gupta family, such as a luxurious apartment in Dubai purchased with the help of the Gupta’s.

Sound Up Pieter Louis
We know there is an R18mil apartment in Burj Khalifa, the tallest building in the world in Dubai. We know that they paid for his wedding at Zimbali, we know that they’ve been footing some of his legal bills.

Voice
SACP Secretary General Blade Nzimande has slammed the president and his son’s roles in what he called the emergence of a parallel shadow state.

Sound Up Blade
The sheer scale of corporate plunder and parasitic plundering of state resources by the Gupta network becomes more and more evident and even more concerning, the central role of president Zuma and his son in auctioning off our national sovereignty is also increasingly apparent.

Voice
And while Duduzane’s business connections assure him of a life in the lap of luxury, ratings agency Moody’s downgraded South Africa late on Friday night and the country is officially in recession.

Sound Up Iraj Abedian
Devi: We are now officially in a recession, you predicted this the last time I saw you?
Iraj: Yes I predicted it unfortunately, but it was technically predictable.

Voice
Economist Dr Iraj Abedian says we are only starting to see the impact of the ratings agencies downgrades on South Africa’s economy, and that the recession could well deepen.

Sound Up Iraj
If it’s not rescued, if recession is not arrested, it goes into a vicious circle. Consumers don’t have the confidence to spend, the investors can see that business is not coming through their doors, they cut back, and the more they cut back the more consumers have less to invest, and it gets into a vicious circle that can pull the economy deeper and deeper into recessionary mindset

Link Devi
Almost everyday there are new developments in the Guptaleaks email saga, and while the emails do raise serious questions around state capture, will any of these allegations hold up in a court of law?

Voice
Associate professor at Wits Law school and practicing advocate Professor James Grant says emails, which are viewed as prima facie evidence by our courts, could well be admitted into evidence in a criminal case, and Duduzane might face criminal charges.

Sound Up James
Devi: Does that mean if you have a relative who holds a high position in government that you can’t do business?
James: No it doesn’t. What the law does though is it places a watch virtually on everyone to say if you suddenly start attracting all sorts of benefits for which you’ve given no real quid pro quo, then you might need to do some explaining. And in fact that’s pretty much the way our prevention of corrupt activities act is framed.

Voice
But criminal charges seem unlikely given the NPA’s current stance on the corruption charges President Zuma still faces

Sound Up James
Devi: But there’s still the 783 charges and the spy tapes saga?
James: Absolutely. It’s mind-boggling. It leaves me speechless, for what it’s worth. I think one had to work very, very hard to try to misunderstand the judgment of the high court, and in my view for what its worth that’s exactly what Jacob Zuma and the NPA are doing in order not to implement the order of the High Court of Pretoria, which is to reinstate the charges.

Voice
Recently Deputy President Cyril Ramaphosa warned that South Africa must guard against becoming a mafia state, but Dr Abedian wonders if we’re entering a new era of colonialisation.

Sound Up Iraj
It’s a colonization of a different nature, in the 21st century, in the daylight, with the full backing of government structures. The very government structures that are entrusted to safeguard.

Sound Up Pieter-Louis
There’s no doubt in my mind, that the Gupta-Zuma nexus very much involves President Jacob Zuma having to make very dubious decisions on how government and government controlled companies manage themselves.
